dict.string: Greenroom arranges Google Chrome windows for you (e.g. tiling a new window to half the screen).

Greenroom puts you in the class picture (your screen with you in it), sends that picture to the Zoom meeting from inside the app, and records it when you press Record, so it needs your camera. It also checks which camera you are facing so it can cut between them. The picture and any recording stay on this Mac, apart from what the meeting itself receives.

Your microphone goes to the Zoom meeting, drives the level meter on the participants panel, and is recorded with the class picture when you record (the file stays on this Mac). With Cues turned on (off by default, macOS 26 only), Greenroom also turns your speech into text on this Mac to suggest links; the audio and the text never leave the Mac and are not saved.
When you press Analyse on a recording, Greenroom turns it into text on this Mac so it can count filler words and pace. It refuses to transcribe at all rather than send the audio to Apple.
